dedupe_keys.name: climate risk and vulnerability assessment in the modernisation of the bratislava zilina kosice railway corridor slovakia

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes how climate change risks were built into the modernisation of Slovakia's main railway corridor from Bratislava through Žilina to Košice, part of the TEN-T core network and Rail Freight Corridor 9. Following the 2018 Methodological Handbook on Assessing Climate Change Impacts on Major Transport Projects, prepared by the Transport Research Centre of Slovakia for the Ministry of Transport and Construction, feasibility studies rated exposure and sensitivity for each railway section and component, such as bridges and tunnels, on a five-level scale from insignificant to catastrophic. Proposed measures include catenary wind-proofing beyond 30 m/s, larger culverts and drainage, raising the alignment above Q100 to Q1000 flood levels, deeper bridge piers, flexible rail fastening against heat, protective walls and windbreaks, plus maintenance, detectors and early warning. Railways of the Slovak Republic (ŽSR) implement them section by section; the Bratislava to Žilina section of about 200 km was almost complete, and the Púchov to Považská Teplá section had a budget of EUR 365 million. The page, first published in 2020 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML. Caveats: the cost of the climate measures is not separated from construction costs, and the section risk maps are not published on the page. The case illustrates hazard exposure screening and climate adaptation for a rail investment; related records are ERA RINF and the UK railway drainage allowances case study.
name: Climate risk and vulnerability assessment in the modernisation of the Bratislava-Žilina-Košice railway corridor, Slovakia
organisations: Ministry of Transport and Construction of the Slovak Republic
outcomes: Each corridor section and component received a five-level climate risk rating, and technical and management measures were written into the project documentation; the Bratislava to Žilina section of about 200 km was almost complete with climate proofing built in.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study from the Slovak Ministry of Transport and Construction and partners
resources_used: Methodological Handbook on Assessing Climate Change Impacts on Major Transport Projects (2018)
Slovak adaptation strategy climate projections RCP 4.5 and 8.5
